Highlights in the attached PDF: an overview of the export process, retention windows by signal type, tamper-evidence mechanisms, and a sample export manifest.

Quick summary:

- Export formats: signed JSON manifest with per-file SHA256, CSV/JSON/Parquet payloads depending on volume and use case.
- Evidence integrity: signed manifests + HSM-backed KMS key signatures + optional notarization via timestamping service.

Samir —

Thanks — happy to confirm details. Answers inline: 

1) Cold-archive exportability & restore SLA:
- Cold archives are exportable on demand. Standard restore SLA for enterprise customers is 48-72 hours for full-archive restores; for smaller, time-bounded slices (day/week/month) typical delivery is 4-12 hours depending on data volume and agreed pre-warm options.
- We provide an exported bundle (payload files + signed manifest) and a retrieval receipt. For very large restores we can stage Parquet snapshots to an S3 bucket (customer-provided or Redwood-temporary) and provide presigned URLs.

2) Tamper evidence and chain-of-custody:
- Customers receive: (a) per-file SHA256 checksums, (b) a signed manifest that lists files, checksums, schema version, time window, and the KMS key id used to sign, and (c) an export receipt with extraction job id, operator id (if manual) and audit timestamp.
- For heightened assurance we support HSM-backed signing and an optional RFC3161 timestamping service to prove the time of signing. We can also provide a notarized digest to an agreed third party.

3) Tenant-scoped slices & pseudonym mapping:
- Yes — we support time-bounded slices by tenant, request-id, or user-id. For privacy we can return either raw internal ids or a pseudonymized mapping table. Pseudonym mapping is deterministic with a tenant-scoped salt and is reversible only with a separate key under customer control (we can deliver mapping only if contractual terms permit).

Additional export details:
- Formats: JSON (line-delimited), CSV (for event logs), Parquet (recommended for large volumes).
- Metadata: export manifest includes schema_version, export_window, signed_by, signed_at, kms_key_fingerprint, and record counts per file.
- Sampling: customers can request full extraction or sampled exports (fixed-rate or stratified by event type) to reduce cost.

Attached: sample-export-manifest.json (anonymized) demonstrating the manifest fields and signature stub.

If you want, we can run a small extraction against your staging tenant and share the anonymized bundle. To proceed we will need a scoped service account and the HubSpot deal id to link the job (so we can record the extraction job id in our audit logs).

One technical addendum on snapshotability and KV cache state:
- If you need full replayability of an inference session including exact KV cache contents, we capture per-request KV snapshots as part of the trace export. For high-throughput tenants this increases export size substantially; typical approach is to include full KV snapshots for flagged requests and delta snapshots for the rest.
- Generating a consistent replay bundle (traces + KV + model variant used) requires a short maintenance window if you want a guaranteed point-in-time capture across many hosts. For most RFP audits we provide a logically-consistent export (reconciled via manifest and per-file sequence numbers) without needing a global lock.

Estimate: small test extract (<=10k events) including KV snapshots: 3-5 hours to produce end-to-end (includes integrity signing and manifest generation). Larger slices scale linearly.

Happy to join a technical call to walk through tradeoffs — propose Wed 10am PT.
